angleRead.name: Noah Tan
angleRead.text: Standing at the corner of College and Alcatraz, watching the way people hunch slightly against the damp chill that's settled in after morning fog. The overcast isn't dramatic—just a persistent gray that makes the neighborhood feel like it's moving through molasses. I want to chase how this specific 49-degree limbo alters the rhythm of the day—who pushes through it, who lets it slow them down, and what small adjustments people make without thinking.
